newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen school gunman sentenced to death.
newsitem.headline: Yemen school gunman sentenced to death.

text.p: A Yemeni gunman was on Monday condemned to face a firing squad for killing a headmistress, a teacher and three children in an attack at two schools on Sunday.
"The court sentences the murderer to execution by firing squad...," the head of a three-judge panel said in a courtroom packed with enraged relatives and friends of the victims.
"The court also decides that the wounded will be treated from his personal funds," the chief judge said, adding that the defendant's property -- a house and a car -- would be confiscated.
Defendant Mohammad Ahmad Misleh appeared calm and said he wished to appeal against the verdict. The prosecutor general said the appeal would be held in public on Tuesday.
The prosecutor general had charged Misleh at the start of the trial on Monday morning with the murder of five people, the attempted murder of 12 others and resisting arrest.
Two court-appointed lawyers defended Misleh, who heard the death sentence in a wheelchair behind the steel bars of a cage in the packed courtroom.

The gunman sustained a leg wound in an exchange of fire with police after he shot an assault rifle at hundreds of students aged six to 18 as they lined up for morning classes at two neighbouring schools in a middle class suburb of the Yemeni capital.
Officials had said earlier that six children were killed in the shooting, but the prosecutor general at the trial said only three were dead and the others were in hospital in critical condition.
Witnesses had described the assailant as a disgruntled former bus driver who had been sacked by the headmistress.
Misleh told the court he had intended to kill the headmistress's husband, alleging that they had approved the kidnap and rape of his eight-year-old daughter 18 months ago.
He said the kidnappers, with whom he had a feud over a plot of land, had also received the approval of the administration at the other school to kidnap his son.
But the prosecutor general produced a medical examiner's report saying the girl was still a virgin and was not raped. There was no independent confirmation of the kidnappings claim.
The girl was brought into the courtroom by the prosecutor. She greeted her father through the steel bars of his cage, but remained silent when the prosecutor asked her questions.
"They told me to say I was insane, but I am not," Misleh, sporting a long, thick beard and wearing a long grey Arab robe, told the judges. He did not say who told him to say that.

Hundreds of people, including most of the families of the victims, crowded into the courtroom. Thousands others, including students from the two schools and their parents, gathered in the street outside the courthouse under heavy security.
